subject: Nova Health dedicated pool — surge readiness & provisioning handoff
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@novahealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kickoff: Nova Health dedicated pool + surge-readiness handoff

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, we're switching this thread into an onboarding handoff so CS/Implementation can coordinate with Ops on provisioning and the surge/autoscale policy. To keep everyone aligned, short checklist and asks below: 

- Confirm target SLOs (latency P95 target you've mentioned is ~120ms in prod).
- Provide 2-week representative traffic CSV (attached) showing baseline vs campaign spikes.
- We propose a baseline pool of 8 A100-equivalent GPUs with burst capacity to 24 for marketing windows (policy options in the attached spreadsheet).
- Autoscale triggers to discuss: GPU util + queue depth vs scheduled promotion windows. We typically recommend a minimum cool-down of 10 mins for burst down to avoid oscillation.
- Regional question: do you require EU fallback routing for DR, or is US-only acceptable for go-live?

I've attached the baseline CSV and a first-pass capacity spreadsheet for ops to review. Grace/Sean — can you take lead on mapping netops constraints and a MAPP (mutual action plan) draft? Kimberly, loop in PM for contract timeline if we need reserved capacity in another region.

Proposed next step: 30-min provisioning working session tomorrow 11:00am PT to align prefixes, KMS, and cache retention. Samir — does that time work?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior CSM, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

Attachments: nova_capacity_baseline.csv, capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@novahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@novahealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-08T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Nova Health dedicated pool + surge-readiness handoff

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the summary. Quick answers inline and a couple of clarifications below.

On Tue, Jun 8, 2026 at 9:12 AM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> - Confirm target SLOs (latency P95 target you've mentioned is ~120ms in prod).

Yes — P95 <= 120ms for short user-facing calls (document retrieval), P95 <= 300ms for background batch embedding jobs.

> - Provide 2-week representative traffic CSV (attached) showing baseline vs campaign spikes.

Attached is the CSV with the last 3 weeks (incl. one promo spike) — peak QPS during promo was ~2.8x baseline, sustained for ~3 hours. We expect a bigger push next month (target campaign) and want the burst margin to be ~3x.

> - Regional question: do you require EU fallback routing for DR, or is US-only acceptable for go-live?

We want EU fallback for compliance-sensitive customers; however, we can accept US-only for the initial soft launch if it shortens time-to-live. Fallback needs to preserve data residency for EU customers (so cross-region KV cache behavior matters).

We can do the 11:00am PT session tomorrow. Please include NetOps and Security.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Director, Platform Engineering — Nova Health
samir.patel@novahealth.com

Attachment: nova_capacity_baseline.csv (updated)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@novahealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-08T11:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Nova Health dedicated pool + surge-readiness handoff

Thanks — looping in design notes and two orthogonal options so we can make a quick tradeoff with Nova: 

Option A (economy-first)
- Baseline pool: 8 GPUs (pinned).
- Autoscale: schedule-based scale-up for promotional windows + reactive scale to 2x baseline when GPU utilization > 70% for 2 consecutive 2-minute samples. Burst cap: 20 GPUs.
- Caching: prefix + KV session cache with 48h retention; warm-up via synthetic prep during scheduled scale-ups.
- Pros: lower steady-state cost. Cons: slower ramp if unexpected spike.

Option B (availability-first)
- Baseline pool: 12 GPUs (pinned).
- Autoscale: reactive scale to queue depth (>50 pending requests) OR GPU util > 60% sustained 1 minute; burst cap: 36 GPUs with 5-min cool-down.
- Caching: longer retention (7d) for KV cache to reduce cold-start token cost for chat sessions.
- Pros: preserves latency during spikes. Cons: higher reserved costs (recommend reserved commitment for EU fallback).

Operational asks for Nova:
- Confirm target cool-down (10 vs 5 min).
- Confirm KMS key for EU vs US if fallback required (we'll need key ARN / contact).
- Provide expected daily session retention (approx # sessions/day).

I've attached capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx with simulation numbers for both options (peak, cost delta, warm-up time). Sean — can you include NetOps constraints and any regional network egress limits before the working session?

Grace O'Connor
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference

On Tue, Jun 8, 2026 at 9:12 AM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Proposed next step: 30-min provisioning working session tomorrow 11:00am PT to align prefixes, KMS, and cache retention.

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@novahealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-09T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Nova Health dedicated pool + surge-readiness handoff

Quick ops check before the meeting:
- NetOps: cross-region failover is doable but requires a reserved minimal pool in EU (recommended 4 GPUs) or a warm-standby with cross-region image sync. Egress caps are 5 Gbps per subnet without an approved increase — if Nova needs higher sustained throughput during EU failover, we need to request quota now.
- Bursting policy: we can support Option B burst cap to 36 GPUs, but to guarantee latency SLO during peak we recommend a short warm-up window and pre-warming of KV caches 20 minutes before a scheduled promo start.
- MAPP: I'll draft a mutual action plan and attach it to the meeting notes — items will include dates for reserved capacity procurement, netops quota ticket number, and security KMS handoff.

Sean Gallagher
Senior Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments (to follow): MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_NH.docx

From: Maria Zhang <maria.zhang@novahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@novahealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-09T12:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Nova Health dedicated pool + surge-readiness handoff

Thanks everyone — after reviewing the options, Nova prefers Option B (availability-first). A couple of asks before the working session: 

1) Please share the MAPP draft and a timeline that includes reserved capacity procurement for EU fallback.
2) Confirm whether 5-minute cool-down is supported; if so we prefer that to keep latency tight.
3) We need Security on the call for KMS alignment.

We'll be ready for the 11:00am PT working session. Can you also include a brief agenda (15m tech, 10m network, 5m next steps)?

Thanks,
Maria Zhang
VP, Product Operations — Nova Health
